Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 80, verse 1–16:

Then we return to what we are accustomed to at the opening of this session, or rather this meeting: verses from the Book of Allah, which we chose to be the verses of the last part (juz') of the Qur'an, because of how often they are repeated by Muslims in their prayers. By the praise and success of Allah, we have finished two surahs: Surah 'Amma and Surah al-Nazi'at. Now we begin the third surah: "He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him" (Surah 'Abasa).

﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him﴾ ['Abasa: 1, 2]. This one who frowned and turned away is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The meaning of ﴿frowned﴾ ('abasa) is that he contracted his face; that is, he showed disapproval with his face.

The meaning of ﴿turned away﴾ (tawalla) is that he showed aversion.

The one meant by "the blind man" in His saying ﴿because the blind man came to him﴾ is 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Umm Maktum (may Allah be pleased with him). He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) before the Hijrah while he was in Makkah, and there were with him some of the great men of Quraysh whose conversion the Prophet (ﷺ) was eager for.

It is well known that when the great men and the nobles embrace Islam, that becomes a cause for the conversion of those beneath them, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) eagerness for them was intense. So this blind man came asking the Prophet (ﷺ), and it is reported that he was saying: "Teach me of what Allah has taught you," and he kept asking the Prophet (ﷺ) to recite to him. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) turned away from him and frowned at him, hoping for and desiring the conversion of these great men. It seems he feared that these great men, the devils, would look down upon the Prophet (ﷺ) if he turned his face to this blind man; it was as if he feared they would hold the Prophet (ﷺ) in contempt if he turned toward such a blind man and turned away from these great men.

So the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), in his frowning and turning away, was observing these two matters. The first matter: hope for the conversion of these great men. The second matter: that they would not look down upon the Prophet (ﷺ) for turning to this blind man, who was despised in their eyes.

There is no doubt that this was an ijtihad (independent judgment) by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and not a contempt for Ibn Umm Maktum. For we know that the Prophet (ﷺ) cared only that his call to the truth spread among the servants of Allah, and that people were equal in his sight; rather, whoever was more eager to accept Islam was more beloved to him. This is what we believe about the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And what will make you know﴾, meaning: what will inform you that this man may purify himself and his faith may grow strong.

﴿Perhaps he may purify himself﴾, meaning: perhaps Ibn Umm Maktum may cleanse himself of sins and of traits that do not befit people like him. If this is what is hoped from him, then he is more deserving of being attended to.

﴿Or he may be reminded, and the reminder benefit him﴾. The meaning: and what will make you know, perhaps he will be reminded, that is, admonished, so the admonition benefits him. For he (may Allah be pleased with him) is more hopeful than those men of being admonished and reminded.

Then He said: ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you attend eagerly. And it is not your concern that he does not purify himself﴾ ['Abasa 5-7]. ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient﴾ means: he thinks himself sufficient through his wealth, for its abundance, and sufficient through his standing, for its strength. To such a one ﴿you attend eagerly﴾, that is, you seek his turning toward you and you turn toward him.

﴿And it is not your concern that he does not purify himself﴾, meaning: there is nothing upon you if this self-sufficient man does not purify himself, for upon you is only the conveying (of the message). Brothers, you see that Allah, glory be to Him, made clear that Ibn Umm Maktum (may Allah be pleased with him) was closer to purification than these great men. He said: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps he may purify himself﴾, and that if these men do not purify themselves despite the Messenger's (peace and blessings be upon him) turning toward them, then there is nothing upon him on their account.

﴿And it is not your concern that he does not purify himself﴾, meaning: there is nothing upon you if he does not purify himself, because his sin is upon him, and upon you is only the conveying.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But as for him who came to you eagerly, and he fears [Allah], from him you are distracted﴾ ['Abasa 8-10]. This is the counterpart of His saying: ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you attend eagerly﴾ ['Abasa 5, 6].

﴿But as for him who came to you eagerly﴾, meaning: hastening, seeking to seize the opportunity of attending the Prophet's (ﷺ) gathering.

﴿And he fears [Allah]﴾, meaning: he fears Allah the Mighty and Majestic in his heart.

﴿From him you are distracted﴾, meaning: you neglect him and ignore him. Why? Because you were occupied with the leaders of the people, hoping they would be guided.

﴿No!﴾, meaning: do not do such a thing. Hence we say that (kalla) here is a particle of prohibition and rebuke, that is: do not do what you have done.

﴿Indeed, it is a reminder﴾. ﴿It﴾ means: the Qur'anic verses which Allah sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿A reminder﴾ that reminds a person of what benefits him and urges him toward it, and informs him of what harms him and warns him against it, and by which the heart is admonished.

﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾ ['Abasa 12], meaning: whoever wills, let him remember the admonition that was sent down and be admonished; and whoever wills, let him not be admonished. This is based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord; so whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve"﴾ [al-Kahf 29]. Allah has given man choice. The choice is by decree (qadar), but in terms of the Law (shar') it is not so. He gave him the choice between believing and disbelieving, but in terms of the Law, He does not approve disbelief for His servants.

Man is not free by the Law to choose between disbelief and belief; rather, he is commanded to believe, and belief is obligatory upon him. But in terms of decree, he is given choice, and he is not, as some people claim, compelled and forced in his actions. Rather, this is an innovated doctrine that the Jabriyyah (determinists) among the Jahmiyyah and others invented, for in reality man is given choice. That is why, if an act occurs without his choice, such as when he is coerced, then his act is not taken into account.

The point is that Allah says: ﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾, meaning: he remembers what was sent down of revelation and is admonished by it; that is, and whoever wills, does not remember it. And the successful is the one whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grants success.

﴿In honored scriptures, exalted, purified, by the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful﴾ ['Abasa 13-16]. That is, this reminder contained in these verses is ﴿in honored scriptures﴾: revered by Allah. The suhuf are the plural of sahifah, and sahifah is that on which speech is written.

These scriptures are ﴿by the hands of safarah﴾. The safarah are the angels, and they were named safarah because they are scribes, derived from al-safar or al-safr, which is a book, as in His saying: ﴿like the donkey carrying books (asfar)﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 5]. It was also said that the safarah are the intermediaries between Allah and His creation, from safir, which is the intermediary between people. From this is the hadith of Abu Rafi' (may Allah be pleased with him), that "the Prophet (ﷺ) married Maymunah before he entered the state of ihram. He said: 'And I was the safir between them'" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (841)], that is, the intermediary.

The point is that the safarah are the angels, and they were named safarah because they are scribes who write, and they were named safarah because they are envoys between Allah and the creation. Jibril (peace be upon him) is an intermediary between Allah and the creation in the descent of revelation, and the scribes who write what a person does also record it and convey it to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while Allah is knowing of it at the time of its writing and before its writing.

﴿By the hands of safarah, noble and dutiful﴾: noble in their character, noble in their creation as well, for they are in the best form and the best conduct. For this reason Allah described the angels as noble scribes who know what you do, and that they, peace be upon them, do not disdain to worship Allah, ﴿and they do not tire; they glorify the night and the day, and they do not slacken﴾ [al-Anbiya' 19, 20].

These verses, as you have heard, contain a discipline from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for creation: that their concern should not be a personal concern but a concern for the good of the cause, and that in calling to Allah they should not prefer a person for his nobility, nor a great man for his greatness, nor a relative for his closeness; rather, people should be equal in their sight in calling to Allah: the poor and the rich, the elder and the younger, the near and the far.

In them is also Allah's gentleness in addressing the Prophet (ﷺ). He said at their beginning: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him﴾. Three verses in which Allah did not address the Prophet (ﷺ) directly, because it is severe rebuke; had it been directed to the Messenger in the second person, it would have carried what it would carry. Instead it came in the third person: ﴿He frowned﴾. Otherwise the situation would have called for: "You frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to you, and what will make you know, perhaps he may purify himself." But He said: ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾.

So He assigned the judgment to the absent party, out of dislike of addressing the Prophet (ﷺ) with these harsh, severe words, and so that those of this nation who might fall into such conduct would not do so. Allah, glory be to Him, described His Mighty Book as being in clear Arabic tongue, and this is part of its clarity.

In the verses there is also evidence for the permissibility of addressing a person by a descriptive epithet such as "the blind," "the lame," or "the one with weak eyesight (al-a'mash)." The scholars used to do this; how often you come across: "al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah," "al-A'mash from Ibn Mas'ud," and so on.

The people of knowledge said: a nickname that refers to a defect is permissible when its purpose is to identify the person, but if its purpose is to shame the person, it is forbidden. For the first, when its purpose is to identify the person, there is a need for it; the second, when its purpose is shaming, is not intended for identification, but only for gloating. It has come in a report: "Do not show gloating over your brother, lest Allah pardon him and test you."[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2506) from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa'.]

We ask Allah for us and for you steadfastness and safety in this world and the Hereafter.

* * *
(...) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By the hands of safarah, noble and dutiful﴾.

Brothers, you see that Allah, glory be to Him, made clear that Ibn Umm Maktum (may Allah be pleased with him) was closer to purification than these great men. He said: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps he may purify himself﴾, and that if these men do not purify themselves despite the Messenger's (peace and blessings be upon him) turning toward them, then there is nothing upon him on their account.

﴿And it is not your concern that he does not purify himself﴾, meaning: there is nothing upon you if he does not purify himself, because his sin is upon him, and upon you is only the conveying.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But as for him who came to you eagerly, and he fears [Allah], from him you are distracted﴾ ['Abasa 8-10]. This is the counterpart of His saying: ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you attend eagerly﴾ ['Abasa 5, 6].

﴿But as for him who came to you eagerly﴾, meaning: hastening, seeking to seize the opportunity of attending the Prophet's (ﷺ) gathering.

﴿And he fears [Allah]﴾, meaning: he fears Allah the Mighty and Majestic in his heart.

﴿From him you are distracted﴾, meaning: you neglect him and ignore him. Why? Because you were occupied with the leaders of the people, hoping they would be guided.

﴿No!﴾, meaning: do not do such a thing. Hence we say that (kalla) here is a particle of prohibition and rebuke, that is: do not do what you have done.

﴿Indeed, it is a reminder﴾. ﴿It﴾ means: the Qur'anic verses which Allah sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿A reminder﴾ that reminds a person of what benefits him and urges him toward it, and informs him of what harms him and warns him against it, and by which the heart is admonished.

﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾ ['Abasa 12], meaning: whoever wills, let him remember the admonition that was sent down and be admonished; and whoever wills, let him not be admonished. This is based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord; so whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve"﴾ [al-Kahf 29]. Allah has given man choice. The choice is by decree (qadar), but in terms of the Law (shar') it is not so. He gave him the choice between believing and disbelieving, but in terms of the Law, He does not approve disbelief for His servants.

Man is not free by the Law to choose between disbelief and belief; rather, he is commanded to believe, and belief is obligatory upon him. But in terms of decree, he is given choice, and he is not, as some people claim, compelled and forced in his actions. Rather, this is an innovated doctrine that the Jabriyyah (determinists) among the Jahmiyyah and others invented, for in reality man is given choice. That is why, if an act occurs without his choice, such as when he is coerced, then his act is not taken into account.

The point is that Allah says: ﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾, meaning: he remembers what was sent down of revelation and is admonished by it; that is, and whoever wills, does not remember it. And the successful is the one whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grants success.

﴿In honored scriptures, exalted, purified, by the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful﴾ ['Abasa 13-16]. That is, this reminder contained in these verses is ﴿in honored scriptures﴾: revered by Allah. The suhuf are the plural of sahifah, and sahifah is that on which speech is written.

These scriptures are ﴿by the hands of safarah﴾. The safarah are the angels, and they were named safarah because they are scribes, derived from al-safar or al-safr, which is a book, as in His saying: ﴿like the donkey carrying books (asfar)﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 5]. It was also said that the safarah are the intermediaries between Allah and His creation, from safir, which is the intermediary between people. From this is the hadith of Abu Rafi' (may Allah be pleased with him), that "the Prophet (ﷺ) married Maymunah before he entered the state of ihram. He said: 'And I was the safir between them'" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (841)], that is, the intermediary.

The point is that the safarah are the angels, and they were named safarah because they are scribes who write, and they were named safarah because they are envoys between Allah and the creation. Jibril (peace be upon him) is an intermediary between Allah and the creation in the descent of revelation, and the scribes who write what a person does also record it and convey it to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while Allah is knowing of it at the time of its writing and before its writing.

﴿By the hands of safarah, noble and dutiful﴾: noble in their character, noble in their creation as well, for they are in the best form and the best conduct. For this reason Allah described the angels as noble scribes who know what you do, and that they, peace be upon them, do not disdain to worship Allah, ﴿and they do not tire; they glorify the night and the day, and they do not slacken﴾ [al-Anbiya' 19, 20].

These verses, as you have heard, contain a discipline from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for creation: that their concern should not be a personal concern but a concern for the good of the cause, and that in calling to Allah they should not prefer a person for his nobility, nor a great man for his greatness, nor a relative for his closeness; rather, people should be equal in their sight in calling to Allah: the poor and the rich, the elder and the younger, the near and the far.

In them is also Allah's gentleness in addressing the Prophet (ﷺ). He said at their beginning: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him﴾. Three verses in which Allah did not address the Prophet (ﷺ) directly, because it is severe rebuke; had it been directed to the Messenger in the second person, it would have carried what it would carry. Instead it came in the third person: ﴿He frowned﴾. Otherwise the situation would have called for: "You frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to you, and what will make you know, perhaps he may purify himself." But He said: ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾.

So He assigned the judgment to the absent party, out of dislike of addressing the Prophet (ﷺ) with these harsh, severe words, and so that those of this nation who might fall into such conduct would not do so. Allah, glory be to Him, described His Mighty Book as being in clear Arabic tongue, and this is part of its clarity.

In the verses there is also evidence for the permissibility of addressing a person by a descriptive epithet such as "the blind," "the lame," or "the one with weak eyesight (al-a'mash)." The scholars used to do this; how often you come across: "al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah," "al-A'mash from Ibn Mas'ud," and so on.

The people of knowledge said: a nickname that refers to a defect is permissible when its purpose is to identify the person, but if its purpose is to shame the person, it is forbidden. For the first, when its purpose is to identify the person, there is a need for it; the second, when its purpose is shaming, is not intended for identification, but only for gloating. It has come in a report: "Do not show gloating over your brother, lest Allah pardon him and test you."[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2506) from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa'.]

We ask Allah for us and for you steadfastness and safety in this world and the Hereafter.

* * *
(...) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By the hands of safarah, noble and dutiful﴾.

Then He, Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿Woe to man! How ungrateful he is!﴾ [Abasa 17]. The word ﴿qutila﴾ (woe, or "may he be destroyed") occurs often in the Qur'an. Some scholars say it means "he is cursed." What appears to be correct is that it means "he is destroyed," because killing (qatl) brings destruction. This is an expression the Arabs use to denounce what a person has become. They say, for example: "So-and-so is destroyed, how bad his character is! So-and-so is destroyed, how wicked he is!" and similar phrases.

As for His saying ﴿Woe to man﴾, some scholars said: the word "man" here refers specifically to the disbeliever, not to every human being, because of His later words ﴿How ungrateful he is!﴾. It is also possible that "man" refers to the human species as a whole, since most of the children of Adam are disbelievers, as is established in the authentic hadith: "Allah says: 'O Adam!' He says on the Day of Resurrection: 'Here I am, at Your service and Your pleasure!' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to him: 'Bring out from your offspring a contingent for the Fire.' He says: 'O Lord, what is the contingent for the Fire?' He says: 'Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3348) and Muslim (222/379), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] All of them are in the Fire, and one out of a thousand is in Paradise. In this case, "man" refers to the species, and the believer is excluded from it by what other texts indicate.

As for His saying ﴿How ungrateful he is!﴾, some scholars said: "how" (ma) here is interrogative (istifham), meaning: "What is it that made him ungrateful? What led him to disbelief?"

Other scholars said: this is an expression of wonder (ta'ajjub), meaning: "How great is his disbelief!" Man's disbelief is great because Allah gave him intellect, sent Messengers to him, sent down Books to him, and supplied him with everything that he needs to believe. Despite all this, he disbelieved, so his disbelief is great.

The difference between the two views is that, according to the first, "how" is interrogative: "What made him so ungrateful?" According to the second, it is exclamatory: "How strange that he disbelieved, when everything is available to him in clarifying the truth and guidance!"

The disbelief mentioned here includes every kind of disbelief, including denial of the Resurrection. Many disbelievers denied resurrection and said: "It is impossible for people to be resurrected after their bones have become decayed," as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And he makes a comparison for Us and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin 78].

Therefore He said: ﴿From what thing did He create him?﴾. This is a rhetorical question (istifham taqrir), meaning: "Affirm what follows it." The verse that follows is ﴿From a drop of semen He created him﴾. In other words: O man, how can you deny the Resurrection? From what were you created? Were you not created from nothing? You were not a thing worth mentioning before, then you came into existence and became a human being. How then can you deny the Resurrection? Therefore He said: ﴿From a drop of semen He created him﴾. The word "nutfah" originally means a small amount of water. Here it means the gushing fluid of the man that comes out from between the spine and the ribs, which he deposits in the womb of the woman, and so she conceives.

﴿From a drop of semen He created him, then He determined him﴾, meaning: He made him pass through stages: a drop (nutfah), then a clot (alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah), as in the authentic hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, who is the truthful and the believed, told us: "Indeed, one of you is gathered together in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clot for a similar period [i.e., forty days as a drop], then he becomes a lump of flesh for a similar period, then an angel is sent to him and breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his term of life, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy. By Him other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm's length between him and it, then the Decree overtakes him and he acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed one of you acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only an arm's length between him and it, then the Decree overtakes him and he acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3208) and Muslim (2643/1).]]

He is determined within his mother's belly. Who determines this determination? Who delivers to him what he grows by, from the blood connected to him through the navel, from his mother's blood? None but Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore He said: ﴿then He determined him﴾.

﴿Then He made the way easy for him﴾. "The way" (sabil) here means the path, that is, He made the path easy for him to come out of his mother's belly into the world of observation.

He also made easy for him, after that, what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two paths﴾ [al-Balad 10]. He made easy for him his mother's two breasts from which he feeds. He made easy for him, after that, what He opened to him of the treasuries of provision. Above all this, He made easy for him what is more important: the path of guidance and success, by sending Messages to him and sending down Books to him.

Then after this: ﴿Then He causes him to die and buries him﴾. Death is the separation of the soul from the body. ﴿Buries him﴾ means He put him in a grave, that is, made him buried as a covering for him and an honour and respect for him. If human beings, when they died, were like other dead creatures, bodies thrown into rubbish heaps, that would be a great humiliation for the dead and for his family. But it is among Allah's blessings, glorified and exalted, that He prescribed this burial for His servants.

Therefore Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said regarding His saying ﴿and buries him﴾: "He honoured him by burying him."

﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him up﴾, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills, ﴿He will raise him up﴾, meaning: He will resurrect him on the Day of Raising up, to recompense him for his deeds.

His saying ﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him up﴾ means that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not unable to raise him up, but the command of Allah has not yet come. Therefore He said: ﴿No! He has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him﴾. The word "lamma" means "lam" (not yet), though it differs from it in some respects. The meaning is that Allah, Exalted, has not yet carried out what He commanded, that is, what He commanded with regard to creation and decree. In other words, the matter has not been completed for the resurrection of this dead person; rather, he has an appointed time that is awaited.

In this there is a refutation of those who deny the Resurrection, who say: "If the Resurrection were true, we would have found our fathers now." This statement of theirs is a baseless and false challenge, because the Messengers never told them: "You will be resurrected now," but they told them: "You will all be resurrected together after you have all died."

Then, Mighty and Majestic, He said, reminding man of what Allah has bestowed on him: ﴿Then let man look at his food. We poured down water in torrents﴾ [Abasa 24–25], meaning: let him look at his food, where it came from, who brought it, and whether anyone created it. No one did.

A person should, at this verse, remember the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who cause it to grow, or are We the Grower? If We willed, We would make it into chaff, and you would be left wondering: "We are burdened with debt! Rather, we are deprived!"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 63–67]. Who caused this crop to grow until it became ripe, and made it easy for us to obtain it so that it became food for us? It is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore He said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it into chaff﴾, after We have brought it forth, We would crush it so that you could not benefit from it.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the rain clouds, or are We the sender? If We willed, We would make it bitter, so why do you not give thanks?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 68–70].

Here He says: ﴿Then let man look at his food﴾, where did it come to him from?

﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾, meaning: from the clouds.

﴿Then We split the earth open﴾, after the rain falls on it, the earth splits open with plants.

﴿Then We caused grain to grow therein﴾, that is, in the earth, ﴿and grapes and herbs, and olives and palm trees, and walled gardens dense with trees, and fruit and pasture﴾ [Abasa 27–31].

﴿Then We caused grain to grow therein﴾, such as wheat, rice, maize, barley, and other many kinds of grain.

﴿And grapes﴾ is well known. ﴿And herbs﴾ is said to be fodder (qatt), which is well known. ﴿Olives﴾ is well known. ﴿Palm trees﴾ likewise. ﴿Walled gardens dense with trees﴾: "hada'iq" is the plural of "hadiqah" (garden), and "ghulb" means having many trees. ﴿And fruit﴾ means what a person enjoys eating of various kinds of fruits. ﴿And pasture﴾: "abb" is a plant well known to the Arabs, which camels graze on.

﴿As provision for you and your cattle﴾ [Abasa 32], meaning: We did that as a enjoyment for you, through which your needs are met, and you also enjoy these blessings by eating the fruits.

Then, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reminded man of his state from the time he was created from a drop until he remained in this world and lived, He mentioned his final state in His saying: ﴿But when the Deafening Blast comes﴾ [Abasa 33], meaning: the great cry that deafens the ears. This is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿On that Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children﴾ [Abasa 34–36]. "His brother" means his full brother, or his brother from the father, or from the mother. "His mother and father" means the direct mother and father, and also the grandfathers and grandmothers. He will flee from all of these. "His wife" means his spouse, and "his children" are the people closest to him and the most beloved to him. He will flee from all of these.

The people of knowledge said: he flees from them lest they demand from him what he neglected of their rights, such as good manners and other things, because on that Day everyone will not love at all for anyone to have a claim against him.

﴿For every one of them on that Day, there will be a matter that will occupy him﴾ [Abasa 37]. Every person is preoccupied with himself and does not look at others. Therefore, when the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "You will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised," Aisha said: "Alas for shame, O Messenger of Allah! Men and women looking at one another?!" The Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "The matter is too grave for them to look at one another."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56).]]

Then Allah divided people on that Day into two groups, saying: ﴿Some faces on that Day will be bright, laughing and joyful﴾ [Abasa 38–39]. "Musfirah" comes from "isfar," which means clarity, because these are the faces of the believers, showing the joy and happiness in their hearts.

﴿Laughing﴾ means smiling, and this is from the perfection of their joy. ﴿Joyful﴾ means they have been given good news, because the angels will receive them with glad tidings, ﴿saying: "Peace be upon you"﴾ [al-Nahl 32].

﴿And other faces on that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will be covered with dust﴾, that is, something like dust, because they are despicable and ugly.

﴿Darkness will cover them﴾ [Abasa 41], that is, gloom.

﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa 42]: those who combined disbelief with wickedness. We ask Allah for well-being. We ask Allah, Exalted, to make us and you among those whose faces are joyful.

What we have said about these verses is not intended as an extended exposition, but as a clarification that brings the meaning closer, because these verses are recited often in the prayers and listened to behind the imams. We ask Allah to make in it a clear victory for us and for you. Indeed He is Generous and Bountiful. May Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.

Then He, Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿Woe to man! How ungrateful he is!﴾ [Abasa 17]. The word ﴿qutila﴾ (woe, or "may he be destroyed") occurs often in the Qur'an. This is an expression the Arabs use to denounce what a person has become. They say, for example: "So-and-so is destroyed, how bad his character is! He made easy for him, after that, what He opened to him of the treasuries of provision. Above all this, He made easy for him what is more important: the path of guidance and success, by sending Messages to him and sending down Books to him.

Death is the separation of the soul from the body. ﴿Buries him﴾ means He put him in a grave, that is, made him buried as a covering for him and an honour and respect for him. If human beings, when they died, were like other dead creatures, bodies thrown into rubbish heaps, that would be a great humiliation for the dead and for his family. But it is among Allah's blessings, glorified and exalted, that He prescribed this burial for His servants.

Therefore Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said regarding His saying ﴿and buries him﴾: "He honoured him by burying him."

He has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him﴾. The word "lamma" means "lam" (not yet), though it differs from it in some respects. Who caused this crop to grow until it became ripe, and made it easy for us to obtain it so that it became food for us? It is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore He said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it into chaff﴾, after We have brought it forth, We would crush it so that you could not benefit from it.

﴿As provision for you and your cattle﴾ [Abasa 32], meaning: We did that as a enjoyment for you, through which your needs are met, and you also enjoy these blessings by eating the fruits.

He will flee from all of these. "His wife" means his spouse, and "his children" are the people closest to him and the most beloved to him. He will flee from all of these.

The people of knowledge said: he flees from them lest they demand from him what he neglected of their rights, such as good manners and other things, because on that Day everyone will not love at all for anyone to have a claim against him.

﴿Darkness will cover them﴾ [Abasa 41], that is, gloom.

﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa 42]: those who combined disbelief with wickedness. We ask Allah for well-being. We ask Allah, Exalted, to make us and you among those whose faces are joyful.

May Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.

He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin 78].

By Him other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm's length between him and it, then the Decree overtakes him and he acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. He made easy for him, after that, what He opened to him of the treasuries of provision. Above all this, He made easy for him what is more important: the path of guidance and success, by sending Messages to him and sending down Books to him.

Then after this: ﴿Then He causes him to die and buries him﴾. Death is the separation of the soul from the body. ﴿Buries him﴾ means He put him in a grave, that is, made him buried as a covering for him and an honour and respect for him. If human beings, when they died, were like other dead creatures, bodies thrown into rubbish heaps, that would be a great humiliation for the dead and for his family. But it is among Allah's blessings, glorified and exalted, that He prescribed this burial for His servants.

Therefore Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said regarding His saying ﴿and buries him﴾: "He honoured him by burying him."

This is an expression the Arabs use to denounce what a person has become. They say, for example: "So-and-so is destroyed, how bad his character is! He made easy for him, after that, what He opened to him of the treasuries of provision. Above all this, He made easy for him what is more important: the path of guidance and success, by sending Messages to him and sending down Books to him.

Death is the separation of the soul from the body. ﴿Buries him﴾ means He put him in a grave, that is, made him buried as a covering for him and an honour and respect for him. If human beings, when they died, were like other dead creatures, bodies thrown into rubbish heaps, that would be a great humiliation for the dead and for his family. But it is among Allah's blessings, glorified and exalted, that He prescribed this burial for His servants.

Therefore Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said regarding His saying ﴿and buries him﴾: "He honoured him by burying him."

He has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him﴾. The word "lamma" means "lam" (not yet), though it differs from it in some respects. Who caused this crop to grow until it became ripe, and made it easy for us to obtain it so that it became food for us? It is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore He said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it into chaff﴾, after We have brought it forth, We would crush it so that you could not benefit from it.

﴿As provision for you and your cattle﴾ [Abasa 32], meaning: We did that as a enjoyment for you, through which your needs are met, and you also enjoy these blessings by eating the fruits.

He will flee from all of these. "His wife" means his spouse, and "his children" are the people closest to him and the most beloved to him. He will flee from all of these.

The people of knowledge said: he flees from them lest they demand from him what he neglected of their rights, such as good manners and other things, because on that Day everyone will not love at all for anyone to have a claim against him.

﴿Darkness will cover them﴾ [Abasa 41], that is, gloom.

﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa 42]: those who combined disbelief with wickedness. We ask Allah for well-being. We ask Allah, Exalted, to make us and you among those whose faces are joyful.

May Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.

Then, Mighty and Majestic, He said, reminding man of what Allah has bestowed on him: ﴿Then let man look at his food. We poured down water in torrents﴾ [Abasa 24–25], meaning: let him look at his food, where it came from, who brought it, and whether anyone created it. No one did.

A person should, at this verse, remember the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who cause it to grow, or are We the Grower? If We willed, We would make it into chaff, and you would be left wondering: "We are burdened with debt! Rather, we are deprived!"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 63–67]. Who caused this crop to grow until it became ripe, and made it easy for us to obtain it so that it became food for us? It is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore He said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it into chaff﴾, after We have brought it forth, We would crush it so that you could not benefit from it.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the rain clouds, or are We the sender? If We willed, We would make it bitter, so why do you not give thanks?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 68–70].

Here He says: ﴿Then let man look at his food﴾, where did it come to him from?

﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾, meaning: from the clouds.

﴿Then We split the earth open﴾, after the rain falls on it, the earth splits open with plants.

﴿Then We caused grain to grow therein﴾, that is, in the earth, ﴿and grapes and herbs, and olives and palm trees, and walled gardens dense with trees, and fruit and pasture﴾ [Abasa 27–31].

﴿Then We caused grain to grow therein﴾, such as wheat, rice, maize, barley, and other many kinds of grain.

﴿And grapes﴾ is well known. ﴿And herbs﴾ is said to be fodder (qatt), which is well known. ﴿Olives﴾ is well known. ﴿Palm trees﴾ likewise. ﴿Walled gardens dense with trees﴾: "hada'iq" is the plural of "hadiqah" (garden), and "ghulb" means having many trees. ﴿And fruit﴾ means what a person enjoys eating of various kinds of fruits. ﴿And pasture﴾: "abb" is a plant well known to the Arabs, which camels graze on.

﴿As provision for you and your cattle﴾ [Abasa 32], meaning: We did that as a enjoyment for you, through which your needs are met, and you also enjoy these blessings by eating the fruits.

Then, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reminded man of his state from the time he was created from a drop until he remained in this world and lived, He mentioned his final state in His saying: ﴿But when the Deafening Blast comes﴾ [Abasa 33], meaning: the great cry that deafens the ears. This is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿On that Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children﴾ [Abasa 34–36]. "His brother" means his full brother, or his brother from the father, or from the mother. "His mother and father" means the direct mother and father, and also the grandfathers and grandmothers. He will flee from all of these. "His wife" means his spouse, and "his children" are the people closest to him and the most beloved to him. He will flee from all of these.

The people of knowledge said: he flees from them lest they demand from him what he neglected of their rights, such as good manners and other things, because on that Day everyone will not love at all for anyone to have a claim against him.

﴿For every one of them on that Day, there will be a matter that will occupy him﴾ [Abasa 37]. Every person is preoccupied with himself and does not look at others. Therefore, when the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "You will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised," Aisha said: "Alas for shame, O Messenger of Allah! Men and women looking at one another?!" The Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "The matter is too grave for them to look at one another."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56).]]

Then Allah divided people on that Day into two groups, saying: ﴿Some faces on that Day will be bright, laughing and joyful﴾ [Abasa 38–39]. "Musfirah" comes from "isfar," which means clarity, because these are the faces of the believers, showing the joy and happiness in their hearts.

﴿Laughing﴾ means smiling, and this is from the perfection of their joy. ﴿Joyful﴾ means they have been given good news, because the angels will receive them with glad tidings, ﴿saying: "Peace be upon you"﴾ [al-Nahl 32].

﴿And other faces on that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will be covered with dust﴾, that is, something like dust, because they are despicable and ugly.

﴿Darkness will cover them﴾ [Abasa 41], that is, gloom.

﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa 42]: those who combined disbelief with wickedness. We ask Allah for well-being. We ask Allah, Exalted, to make us and you among those whose faces are joyful.

What we have said about these verses is not intended as an extended exposition, but as a clarification that brings the meaning closer, because these verses are recited often in the prayers and listened to behind the imams. We ask Allah to make in it a clear victory for us and for you. Indeed He is Generous and Bountiful. May Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.

Then He, Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿Woe to man! How ungrateful he is!﴾ [Abasa 17]. The word ﴿qutila﴾ (woe, or "may he be destroyed") occurs often in the Qur'an. Some scholars say it means "he is cursed." What appears to be correct is that it means "he is destroyed," because killing (qatl) brings destruction. This is an expression the Arabs use to denounce what a person has become. They say, for example: "So-and-so is destroyed, how bad his character is! So-and-so is destroyed, how wicked he is!" and similar phrases.

As for His saying ﴿Woe to man﴾, some scholars said: the word "man" here refers specifically to the disbeliever, not to every human being, because of His later words ﴿How ungrateful he is!﴾. It is also possible that "man" refers to the human species as a whole, since most of the children of Adam are disbelievers, as is established in the authentic hadith: "Allah says: 'O Adam!' He says on the Day of Resurrection: 'Here I am, at Your service and Your pleasure!' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to him: 'Bring out from your offspring a contingent for the Fire.' He says: 'O Lord, what is the contingent for the Fire?' He says: 'Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3348) and Muslim (222/379), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] All of them are in the Fire, and one out of a thousand is in Paradise. In this case, "man" refers to the species, and the believer is excluded from it by what other texts indicate.

As for His saying ﴿How ungrateful he is!﴾, some scholars said: "how" (ma) here is interrogative (istifham), meaning: "What is it that made him ungrateful? What led him to disbelief?"

Other scholars said: this is an expression of wonder (ta'ajjub), meaning: "How great is his disbelief!" Man's disbelief is great because Allah gave him intellect, sent Messengers to him, sent down Books to him, and supplied him with everything that he needs to believe. Despite all this, he disbelieved, so his disbelief is great.

The difference between the two views is that, according to the first, "how" is interrogative: "What made him so ungrateful?" According to the second, it is exclamatory: "How strange that he disbelieved, when everything is available to him in clarifying the truth and guidance!"

The disbelief mentioned here includes every kind of disbelief, including denial of the Resurrection. Many disbelievers denied resurrection and said: "It is impossible for people to be resurrected after their bones have become decayed," as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And he makes a comparison for Us and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin 78].

Therefore He said: ﴿From what thing did He create him?﴾. This is a rhetorical question (istifham taqrir), meaning: "Affirm what follows it." The verse that follows is ﴿From a drop of semen He created him﴾. In other words: O man, how can you deny the Resurrection? From what were you created? Were you not created from nothing? You were not a thing worth mentioning before, then you came into existence and became a human being. How then can you deny the Resurrection? Therefore He said: ﴿From a drop of semen He created him﴾. The word "nutfah" originally means a small amount of water. Here it means the gushing fluid of the man that comes out from between the spine and the ribs, which he deposits in the womb of the woman, and so she conceives.

﴿From a drop of semen He created him, then He determined him﴾, meaning: He made him pass through stages: a drop (nutfah), then a clot (alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah), as in the authentic hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, who is the truthful and the believed, told us: "Indeed, one of you is gathered together in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clot for a similar period [i.e., forty days as a drop], then he becomes a lump of flesh for a similar period, then an angel is sent to him and breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his term of life, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy. By Him other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm's length between him and it, then the Decree overtakes him and he acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed one of you acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only an arm's length between him and it, then the Decree overtakes him and he acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3208) and Muslim (2643/1).]]

He is determined within his mother's belly. Who determines this determination? Who delivers to him what he grows by, from the blood connected to him through the navel, from his mother's blood? None but Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore He said: ﴿then He determined him﴾.

﴿Then He made the way easy for him﴾. "The way" (sabil) here means the path, that is, He made the path easy for him to come out of his mother's belly into the world of observation.

He also made easy for him, after that, what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two paths﴾ [al-Balad 10]. He made easy for him his mother's two breasts from which he feeds. He made easy for him, after that, what He opened to him of the treasuries of provision. Above all this, He made easy for him what is more important: the path of guidance and success, by sending Messages to him and sending down Books to him.

Then after this: ﴿Then He causes him to die and buries him﴾. Death is the separation of the soul from the body. ﴿Buries him﴾ means He put him in a grave, that is, made him buried as a covering for him and an honour and respect for him. If human beings, when they died, were like other dead creatures, bodies thrown into rubbish heaps, that would be a great humiliation for the dead and for his family. But it is among Allah's blessings, glorified and exalted, that He prescribed this burial for His servants.

Therefore Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said regarding His saying ﴿and buries him﴾: "He honoured him by burying him."

﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him up﴾, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills, ﴿He will raise him up﴾, meaning: He will resurrect him on the Day of Raising up, to recompense him for his deeds.

His saying ﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him up﴾ means that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not unable to raise him up, but the command of Allah has not yet come. Therefore He said: ﴿No! He has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him﴾. The word "lamma" means "lam" (not yet), though it differs from it in some respects. The meaning is that Allah, Exalted, has not yet carried out what He commanded, that is, what He commanded with regard to creation and decree. In other words, the matter has not been completed for the resurrection of this dead person; rather, he has an appointed time that is awaited.

This statement of theirs is a baseless and false challenge, because the Messengers never told them: "You will be resurrected now," but they told them: "You will all be resurrected together after you have all died."
